q: Can an EU importer sell back unused CBAM certificates, and what happens to them after a year?
title: Selling back unused CBAM certificates
short: Partly. An authorised CBAM declarant can ask the Commission to repurchase certificates left over after the annual surrender, within a cap and a deadline set in Article 23. Certificates that are neither surrendered nor repurchased in time are cancelled under Article 24. They cannot be sold to other importers.

p: After the annual declaration and surrender, the declarant can request that the Commission buy back excess certificates still in its registry account. The Regulation sets the repurchase price and caps how many certificates can be repurchased, so buying well above need can mean money lost. Check the current consolidated text of Article 23 for the price and the cap.

Certificates still in the account after the surrender and repurchase window are cancelled by the Commission. Check the current consolidated text of Article 24 for which certificates are cancelled, when, and whether any payment applies.

CBAM certificates are not EU ETS allowances. They are sold by a central platform to authorised declarants only, and cannot be traded or transferred between declarants. The only exits are surrender, repurchase or cancellation.

Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 moved the annual declaration and surrender to 30 September of the following year and started certificate sales in February 2027 for 2026 imports. The repurchase and cancellation timing moved with it. Take the exact dates from the consolidated CBAM Regulation before planning purchases.

example.title: Worked example: how much might be sold back (illustrative)
lines: Compare the 200 with the repurchase cap in the current Article 23: only certificates within the cap can be repurchased
example.note: Anything above the cap and not surrendered faces cancellation under Article 24.
